newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BIDS TOTAL HUF30.5BLN FOR PANNON HUF24BLN BONDS.
newsitem.headline: BIDS TOTAL HUF30.5BLN FOR PANNON HUF24BLN BONDS.

text.p: Hungarian mobile telephone company Pannon GSM's auction on Thursday of inflation-indexed bonds totalling 24 billion forints nominal value received 30.5 billion forints worth of bids, the issue manager ING Barings said.
"We received bids totalling 30.5 billion forints for the 24 billion forints par value bonds," Farbod Lotfi, Director of the issue manager ING Barings Rt told Reuters.
Pannon auctioned three-year (series A), four-year (series B) and five-year (series C) bonds of eight billion forints nominal value for each series.
"Each series saw oversubscription of at least 20 percent," Lotfi said. "There were 50 ot 55 bids for each with 48 bids accepted -- the public hand (minimum number of bids necessary) was reached."
Lotfi added the Council of the Budapest Stock Exchange would decide on a flotation of the bonds for March 3.

The bonds bear an interest rate of year-on-year CPI plus three percent, to be adjusted semi-annually, with interest added to the capital annually and the interest and capital to be paid on the day of maturity.
Series A bonds mature on February 25, 2000, series B on February 26, 2001 and series C on February 26, 2002.
Capital and interest repayment is guaranteed by ING Bank NV and the maximum permitted oversubscription is nine billion forints.

For Series A, 9.9 billion forints of bids arrived and 8.188 billion forints worth were accepted. The minimum price was 100.05 percent of par value, the maximum was 102.9111 percent and the average 100.2651 percent, Lotfi said.

For Series B, 10.45 billion forints of bids arrived and 8.153 billion forints worth were accepted. The minimum price was 100.1 percent of par value, the maximum was 102.3111 percent and the average 100.3692.

For Series C, 9.82 billion forints of bids arrived and 8.63 billion forints worth were accepted. The minimum price was 100.01 percent of par value, the maximum was 102.1111 percent and the average 100.2271 percent, Lotfi said.

Pannon, which forecasts its number of subscribers to reach 308,000 by the end of 1997 from 170,000 at the end of 1996, plans to spend most of the money raised on infrastructure development, the company said.
"We plan to use 80 percent of the amount raised towards network expansion," said Gussi Emri, Pannon GSM General Director, said last week.
